items.title: BREAKTHROUGH: IISc Bengaluru Designs a Moon Habitat Bigger Than the ISS That Fits in One Rocket
items.summary:
IISc Bengaluru has designed a modular moon habitat that fits inside a single rocket, potentially reshaping the future of space exploration.

Researchers at IISc have proposed the BHEEM habitat, a modular system designed to support a crew of 16 for long-term lunar or Martian missions. By utilising a clever architecture of triangular, square, and pentagonal panels connected by specialised joints, the design maximises internal living space while simplifying assembly. This approach represents a significant shift in India’s strategy, moving from purely engineering-focused goals to solving complex human factors and logistics challenges in space.

The structure is designed to fit inside a single 800 cubic meter payload, such as a SpaceX Starship, before expanding to offer over 2,000 cubic meters of usable volume. Finite element analysis confirms the structural integrity of the design, which uses space-grade titanium alloys to withstand lunar conditions. As nations increasingly compete in the space race, this habitat concept offers a scalable solution for sustainable, long-term habitation beyond Earth.

items.summary: In episode 1023 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Aishwarya Srinivasan, Co-Founder of The Gen Academy about the crucial founder mindset for AI startups, emphasizing flexibility, knowing when to pivot, and holding strong opinions loosely. This approach helps them navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape and build truly defensible companies.

items.title: BREAKING: ISRO Launches India's First Satellite That Can Watch the Entire Country Every 30 Minutes
items.summary:
ISRO is launching a satellite that can monitor the entire Indian landmass every 30 minutes. Essential space news.

The upcoming mission, designated EOS-05, aims to provide persistent Earth observation from a geostationary orbit. Unlike standard imaging technology, this satellite maintains a fixed view of the region, enabling rapid repeat imaging of fast-moving events like cyclones and floods. This capability represents a significant advancement in how we track environmental changes across the country.

We break down the technical specifications, including the multispectral and hyperspectral imaging capabilities that support applications in agriculture and national security. By providing real-time data, this launch marks a major milestone in India news, building on lessons learned from previous missions to ensure reliable performance in orbit.

items.title: ALERT: Elon Musk Tells G20 AI Will Face a Global Power Crisis Within the Next Year
items.summary:
Elon Musk warns that global AI growth faces an imminent energy crisis, with power demand outstripping supply as early as next year.

Addressing ministers at the G20, Musk highlighted how the rapid expansion of data centres is creating a massive power bottleneck. With current infrastructure struggling to keep pace with chip production, he predicts a severe energy deficit that could hinder the next phase of development. This analysis unpacks the core conflict between software scaling and raw electrical capacity.

Beyond energy constraints, Musk projects that artificial intelligence will reach professional coding proficiency within 18 months, potentially adding trillions in economic output. We examine how this shift in future technology priorities is forcing nations to rethink their grid investments and data centre strategies. Understanding these physical limits is essential for anyone following the latest AI news updates.

items.title: EXPOSED: Anthropic's New Model Solved a 5 Year Bug and Admitted Its AI Accessed Real Servers
items.summary:
Anthropic Claude 5.1 has launched, marking a shift toward autonomous agents and improved infrastructure governance.

This release introduces Fable 5.1 for general enterprise use and Mythos 5.1 for high-security sectors. We examine how these models are moving beyond simple chatbots to handle complex, long-running tasks, such as the 38-hour run performed by RAMP. The update also addresses previous security concerns with new real-time classifiers and isolated sandbox environments.

Beyond technical capabilities, Anthropic is reshaping AI model pricing to improve context economics. By reducing context cache reads to $0.25 per million tokens, enterprises can expect significant cost reductions. We also look at the real-world impact of this technology, including how the model helped solve a complex software bug that had persisted for five years.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Zoho Just Built the Platform That Lets One Developer Replace an Entire DevOps Team
items.summary:
Zoho Catalyst 3.0 Challenges Cloud Giants: Anand Nergunam Discusses Zoho Growth

While generative AI coding assistants have made writing code lightning-fast, taking applications from a working prompt to production-ready deployment still involves fragmented cloud infrastructure, multi-vendor integrations, and complex DevOps bottlenecks. Zoho, a bootstrapped, profitable Indian tech giant with over 19,000 employees, has launched Catalyst 3.0—a serverless, full-stack developer platform designed to bridge the gap between AI coding assistants and live deployment.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Anand Nergunam, Global Vice President of Revenue Growth at Zoho, to explore how Catalyst 3.0 takes on global cloud infrastructure platforms like AWS Amplify, Supabase, and Vercel. They discuss removing friction in AI-assisted developer workflows, preventing token maxing with machine-readable documentation, Zoho's full-stack vision spanning chip-to-cloud infrastructure, offering free access to students, and how AI is transforming developer roles into business problem solvers.

Can an integrated, full-stack serverless platform redefine developer productivity for the AI era?

Zoho Catalyst 3.0 Challenges Cloud Giants: Anand Nergunam Discusses Zoho Growth

While generative AI coding assistants have made writing code lightning-fast, taking applications from a working prompt to production-ready deployment still involves fragmented cloud infrastructure, multi-vendor integrations, and complex DevOps bottlenecks. Zoho, a bootstrapped, profitable Indian tech giant with over 19,000 employees, has launched Catalyst 3.0—a serverless, full-stack developer platform designed to bridge the gap between AI coding assistants and live deployment.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Anand Nergunam, Global Vice President of Revenue Growth at Zoho, to explore how Catalyst 3.0 takes on global cloud infrastructure platforms like AWS Amplify, Supabase, and Vercel. They discuss removing friction in AI-assisted developer workflows, preventing token maxing with machine-readable documentation, Zoho's full-stack vision spanning chip-to-cloud infrastructure, offering free access to students, and how AI is transforming developer roles into business problem solvers.

Can an integrated, full-stack serverless platform redefine developer productivity for the AI era?

items.title: Kargo in Action
items.summary:
Meet the Akuity engineers who built Kargo and wrote this book, Ken Cochrane, Jesse Suen, and Kent Rancourt. 

Kargo is a Kubernetes-native application lifecycle orchestration tool that works alongside Argo CD to promote software builds, automatically moving software artifacts, container images, Helm chart versions, or Git commits from development to staging to production.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
1. Why isn't traditional CI/CD enough for modern software delivery?
2. Why should teams separate deployment from promotion?
3. How does Kargo close the gap between building software and running it safely?
4. How can teams promote the same artifact across multiple environments?
5. What is a promotion control plane, and why do teams need one?
6. How can teams add approvals without slowing every release?
7. How does Kargo make software promotions auditable?
8. How can teams trace exactly what reached each environment?
9. How does Kargo make rollbacks safer and more predictable?
10. How can teams coordinate promotions across multiple services?
11. How does Kargo work with existing GitOps tools like Argo CD?
12. How can teams customize promotion workflows without creating fragile scripts?
13. How does Kargo help organizations balance delivery speed with governance?
14. How does Kargo compare to other similar tools?
15. What is the difference between the free version of Kargo and the paid version?

This is a live, interactive session, feel free to add your questions in the comments.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #KARGO to enter the raffle!
